paragraphs: My name is Tom, and I am twelve years old. On Saturday evening, Dad, Lily, and I went to the night market. It is near the park, and it is open on two nights. A big sign stood at the gate. It said, "Night Market: Friday and Saturday. Open from five o'clock to midnight. The last night is on the fifth of December." "That is the date to remember," said Dad. "Today we must go home at eight o'clock."

At the first food stall, there was a second sign. It said, "Pizza with olives: sixty baht." Under that, it said, "Fruit juice: twenty baht." The last line said, "Rice with chicken: forty baht." Lily looked at the sign and looked unhappy. "The sign is badly painted," she said. "Is the juice twenty baht or seventy baht?" I came near and looked again.

"It is twenty," I said, "because the first number is two." Dad asked the man, "Is the juice twenty baht?" "Yes," said the man, "and the pizza is sixty." We wanted one pizza and two juices. "That is one hundred baht," said Dad. "Tom, please fetch my money from the bag." I fetched the money and gave it to Dad. Dad paid one hundred baht.

"Your pizza will be ready soon," said the man. Lily smelled the olives and smiled. We sat on a bench and had dinner together. At eight o'clock, we walked home. The night market was still busy until midnight. Prices, times, and dates are on every sign. We read them, and we know when and how much.
text.summary: Tom, Lily, and Dad go to the night market. A sign gives the times, the dates, and the prices, and they buy a pizza with olives and two juices.
